prize_parts.citation: For the development of optical lattice clocks and their extraordinary precision in tests of fundamental physics.

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks turn precision spectroscopy into a durable new measurement capability. Katori and Ye made complementary contributions, and the achievement has been demonstrated and refined across laboratories. Its importance lies both in precision timekeeping and in enabling sensitive tests of fundamental physics and new approaches such as geodesy. This is a mature experimental advance with consequences beyond the clock itself.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is whether the prize should recognize an instrument whose most consequential applications are still developing. The clock's extraordinary precision emerged through cumulative technical progress, so the boundary between the foundational achievement and later refinements needs careful definition.

responses.point: Olsson finds the clock achievement consequential but asks whether its defining contribution is the concept, its precision milestones, or a later application.
responses.response: I would center the citation on the optical lattice clock and the measurement precision it made possible, rather than on any single later application. The underlying clock advance is already established across laboratories, while its applications strengthen the case without needing to define it.

responses.point: Johansson notes the difficulty of separating foundational clock concepts from the technical improvements that reached the stated precision.
responses.response: That is a real attribution problem, but it does not erase the identifiable complementary contributions of Katori and Ye to the clock approaches. I would keep the scope on the development of optical lattice clocks and their precision measurement capability, rather than treating every subsequent improvement as part of the discovery.

responses.point: Danielsson questions whether optical lattice clocks have yet reached the impact of a prize-level discovery rather than that of a major precision instrument.
responses.response: A new measurement instrument can be prizeworthy when it changes what can be tested and measured. Here the clocks enable sensitive tests of fundamental physics, and their reproducible precision gives them a scientific role beyond improved timekeeping alone.

uncertainties: Which fundamental tests or applications will prove most consequential over the long term remains open.
The historical boundary between the foundational clock concepts and later precision improvements needs review.
